exposure: Comparison between first and subsequent pregnancies
Presence or absence of pre-existing chronic conditions in VAMA primiparae
Very advanced maternal age (VAMA, ≥45 years old)
Maternal age within VAMA group (45-49 vs. ≥50 years)
cohort: 222 primiparous women aged ≥45 (VAMA) compared to 222 primiparous women aged 30-35, delivering at Sheba Medical Center from 2008 to 2013
finding: Primiparity at VAMA is an independent risk factor for adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes, including GDM, GHTN, preeclampsia-eclampsia, preterm delivery, cesarean birth, and low birth weight, even in the absence of chronic medical conditions or with the use of a young oocyte donor.
mod_finding: VAMA primiparae were more likely to deliver by cesarean birth compared to younger primiparae.
